It marked the return of ESL One to Birmingham, who last hosted the event in [[ESL_One/Birmingham/2019|2019]]. The tournament began competitively, with no clear favourite. Team Falcons, however, gained momentum the quickest, and they beat [[BetBoom Team]] 3-0 in an ill-tempered Grand Final. The qualification process of ESL One Birmingham 2024 saw difficulties. Several players from Russia and Belarus were unable to obtain visas to enter the United Kingdom. The team most affected by this was [[1win]]. Despite deadline extensions, [[#1win visa issues and OG invite controversy|ESL eventually removed them from the event]], and sought a replacement, eventually settling on [[OG]]. This choice was controversial, as this deprived Eastern Europe of a team, but also allowed OG an opportunity to qualify for [[Riyadh Masters/2024|Riyadh Masters 2024]]. The event proved to be highly-successful for ESL. Esports Charts reported that the event broke several viewership records for any ESL One event, and reached mainstream coverage from the BBC and Sky News. {{Quote|There is just not one weak point in this team. It marked the return of ESL One to Birmingham, who last hosted the event in [[ESL_One/Birmingham/2019|2019]]. ESL One was set to return to Birmingham in [[ESL_One/Birmingham/2020|2020]], only for the COVID-19 pandemic to halt those plans, and the event was converted into a set of online-only regional tournaments. Unlike the [[ESL_One/Birmingham/2018|2018]] and 2019 editions, the event took place in the [[wikipedia:bp_pulse_LIVE|Resorts World Arena]], on the outskirts of Birmingham city centre. The event received £3m of funding from the UK government and local authorities, taken from a fund from the [[wikipedia:2022 Commonwealth Games|2022 Commonwealth Games]] to promote cultural and sporting events.{{cite web|url=https://esportsinsider.com/2024/01/esl-one-birmingham-wmca-uk-government-funding|title=ESL One Birmingham receives funding from WMCA and UK Government|author=Jonno Nicholson|publisher=Esports Insider|date=2024-01-03}} The top four of the [[ESL Pro Tour]] at the start of the qualifiers, [[Gaimin Gladiators]], [[BetBoom Team]], [[Xtreme Gaming]] and [[Team Liquid]] were invited directly to the event, and the remainder of the slots were filled with regional qualifiers. However, several players from Russia and Belarus were unable to obtain visas to enter the United Kingdom. [[Team Falcons]]' [[Malr1ne]] obtained his visa, but was late, so [[SumaiL]] stood in for them initially. The team most affected by this, however, was [[1win]]. Despite deadline extensions, [[#1win visa issues and OG invite controversy|ESL eventually removed them from the event]], and sought a replacement, eventually settling on [[OG]]. This choice was controversial, as this deprived Eastern Europe of a team, but also allowed OG an opportunity to qualify for [[Riyadh Masters/2024|Riyadh Masters 2024]]. The event began highly-competitively, with no clear strongest team in either Group A or Group B. Last season's dominant team, [[Gaimin Gladiators]], fell in Group B with a 4-6 score, with first-placed OG progressing with a 6-4 score, showcasing how close the teams were. The International 2023 champions [[Team Spirit]] finished with a 5-5 score in the same group, forcing a four-way tiebreaker with [[Tundra Esports]], [[Xtreme Gaming]] and [[HEROIC]], which saw Team Spirit eliminated and Tundra Esports securing an Upper Bracket spot. The Grand Final was contested between [[Team Falcons]] and [[BetBoom Team]]. Things had been fractious between the two teams, with [[TORONTOTOKYO]] first allegedly making offensive comments before the Grand Finals of [[DreamLeague/Season 22|DreamLeague Season 22]],{{cite web|url=https://www.esports.net/news/dota/atf-confirms-no-beef-with-torontotokyo-after-dreamleague/|title=ATF Confirms No Beef with TORONTOTOKYO After DreamLeague|author=Marcus Wong|publisher=Esports.net|date=2024-03-14}} which Team Falcons won 3-0. TORONTOTOKYO reignited the drama during the event, supposedly refusing to shake hands after the Grand Final.{{cite web|url=https://www.esports.net/news/dota/team-falcons-handshake-snub-betboom-dota-beef/|title=Falcons handshake snub at ESL One Birmingham 2024: Is there beef with BetBoom?|author=Marcus Wong|publisher=Esports.net|date=2024-04-30}} However, BetBoom Team seemingly lost the plot mentally during the Grand Final, with Team Falcons grinding BetBoom Team to a 3-0 win, with game 3 being extremely one-sided. This also extended Team Falcons' streak over BetBoom Team across all tournaments to 5 series wins and 2 draws. Away from the game, lighter moments from the event focused on the rather large quantities of alcohol being consumed, usually a glass being downed in one go while the crowd cheered on the drinker.{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/ESLDota2/posts/eslone-birmingham-in-a-nutshell/812445384245872/|title=#ESLOne Birmingham in a nutshell:|author=ESL Dota 2|date=2024-04-28}} The {{U|Kobold Foreman}}, whose animation involved drinking from a glass aggressively, became an unofficial mascot of the event.{{cite web|url=https://reddit.com/r/DotA2/comments/1cfftqq/pov_you_are_unfamiliar_with_the_kobold_meme_and/|title=POV: You are unfamiliar with the Kobold meme and see this reaction at ESL Birmingham|author=ricchi_|date=2024-04-28}} UK-born [[Ari]], playing for [[OG]], was also cheered on enthusastically by the crowd in the stadium, and was one of the most-sought after interviewees at the event.{{cite web|url=https://medium.com/@mikehasswriting_48994/ari-if-i-had-to-choose-between-being-known-as-the-best-player-or-a-great-teammate-id-rather-be-6f5bc874dc4e|title=Ari: “If I had to choose between being known as the best player, or a great teammate, I’d rather be known as the best player”|author=Michael Hassall|date=2024-05-02}} The event proved to be highly-successful for ESL. Esports Charts reported that the event had the highest total viewers of any ESL One event, nearly 44% more than [[ESL One/Kuala Lumpur/2023|ESL One Kuala Lumpur 2023]], and the third-highest concurrent views of any ESL One event.{{cite web|url=https://escharts.com/news/esl-one-birmingham-2024-viewership|title=ESL One Birmingham 2024 becomes most watched tournament of the series|author=Dmytro Murko|publisher=Esports Charts|date=2024-04-29}} The event also reached mainstream coverage, with the BBC{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/newsbeat-68919773|title=ESL One Birmingham kicks off bumper esports season in UK|author=Andrew Rogers|publisher=BBC|date=2024-04-29}} and Sky News{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DpsgytS5YIo|title=Thousands of fans head to West Midlands to watch professional video gamers|publisher=Sky News|date=2024-04-28}} reporting on the event. [[Jenkins]], a talent at the event, was also interviewed by Sky News.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/SkyNews/status/1784567444134109272|title='A million dollar prize is not that high for esports.'|author=Sky News|date=2024-04-28}} ===1win visa issues and OG invite controversy=== Several Russian and Belarusian players who were set to attend the event faced visa issues, caused by sanctions applied as a result of the [[wikipedia:Russo-Ukrainian War|Russo-Ukrainian War]] and the [[wikipedia:Poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal|Salisbury poisonings]]. These notably impacted the younger players, with fewer career earnings and limited travel history. [[Team Falcons]]' [[Malr1ne]] managed to obtain his visa, but it was delayed, requiring [[SumaiL]] to stand-in for them at the event at the start. [[1win]], however, faced the greatest issues. The team had qualified from the [[ESL_One/Birmingham/2024/Eastern_Europe/Closed_Qualifier|Eastern European qualifiers]], giving them less time to prepare for their visas, and had accomplished less in ''Dota 2'' compared with the likes of [[Team Spirit]] and [[BetBoom Team]], making their visa applications more likely to be rejected. ESL extended their deadline multiple times, but were eventually forced to cancel their invite. ESL reached out to the next Eastern European team in the qualifiers, [[Virtus.pro]] (as well as, reportedly, [[Entity]]{{cite web|url=https://escorenews.com/en/dota-2/news/57619-chinese-community-is-unhappy-with-og-invite-to-birmingham-2024-as-it-decreases-chances-for-g2-ig-and-azure-ray|title=Chinese community is unhappy with OG invite to Birmingham 2024, as it decreases chances for G2.iG and Azure Ray|publisher=Escorenews.com|date=2024-04-10}}) but they were also unable to participate at such short notice. ESL then used their EPT rankings to determine the next eligible team that could attend, which was [[OG]], who had the documentation to enter the United Kingdom.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/ESLDota2/status/1777600574231343161|title=Important update regarding #ESLOne Birmingham:|author=ESL Dota2|date=2024-04-09}} 1win's coach, [[Ahilles]], however, was unhappy with the decision, as ESL's decision was taken just two hours before 1win actually received their visas. Additionally, the final ESL extension deadline fell on a weekend, when no consulate was open, meaning the extension was not truly an extension.{{cite web|url=https://afkgaming.com/dota2/news/esl-one-birmingham-2024-1win-claims-having-no-visa-issues-as-esl-hands-slot-to-og|title=ESL One Birmingham 2024: 1win Claims Having No Visa Issues as ESL Hands Slot to OG|author=Dorjee Palzang|publisher=AFK Gaming|date=2024-04-09}}{{cite web|url=https://esports.gg/news/dota-2/esl-one-birmingham-1wins-situation-and-chinese-community/|title=ESL Birmingham: Chinese Dota community dissatisfied with ESL after OG replace 1win|author=Shiqi Chen|publisher=Esports.gg|date=2024-04-09}}{{cite web|url=https://telegra.ph/Oficialnaya-poziciya-1win-o-reshenii-ESL-snyat-komandu-c-ESL-One-Birmingham-2024-04-09|title=Официальная позиция 1win о решении ESL снять команду c ESL One Birmingham 2024|trans_title=Official position of 1win on the ESL decision to remove the team from ESL One Birmingham 2024|language={{Flag|ru}} Russian|author=1win|date=2024-04-09}} The decision to hand the slot to [[OG]] was itself controversial. OG had failed to qualify for ESL One Birmingham 2024 and [[DreamLeague/Season 23|DreamLeague Season 23]], meaning their [[ESL_Pro_Tour/Leaderboard/Season_2|EPT points]] were stuck at 2,296, and although they were in the top 8 in the standings (granting them qualification to [[Riyadh Masters/2024|Riyadh Masters 2024]]), they were likely to be overtaken by multiple teams who qualified to either ESL One Birmingham 2024 and/or DreamLeague Season 23. By taking part in ESL One Birmingham 2024, however, it gave OG the opportunity to secure their invite. This impacted not only OG and 1win, but also [[G2 x iG]], another team in the vicinity of the top 8, who now had to compete against OG as well. At ESL One Birmingham 2024, OG finished 4th, securing themselves 3,200 points — not quite enough to guarantee themselves top 8 overall, but likely.{{cite web|url=https://reddit.com/r/DotA2/comments/1cfft4b/dreamleague_s23_final_invites_permutations/|title=DreamLeague S23 Final Invites Permutations|author=[[noxville]]|date=2024-04-28}} Results during
